title: Chapter 96: Game Start
html:
Even Chen Ge disliked lingering in the Sealed Classroom, yet Fei Youliang and Zhu Jianing walked straight inside. A strange odor hung in the air. Crossing the threshold felt like sinking underwater; an invisible pressure settled over them and made their breathing uneven.

“Youliang, should I wait outside?” The classroom was darker than the corridor. Behind Fei Youliang, Zhu Jianing grimaced with fear, sweat covering his brow.

“What did we promise before coming in? We said we wouldn’t abandon each other, and you’re already giving up?” Fei Youliang grew increasingly irritable. The uniforms looked no different from horror-film props, yet something made him reluctant to approach them.

Zhu Jianing did not notice that his teammate’s confidence had been shattered. He whispered from behind him, “Where do you think the Haunted House’s worker will be hiding? Will they jump up from underneath the uniforms?”

“I’m not sure, but that would be the obvious trick.” Fei Youliang edged toward the lectern. His fists clenched as he passed between the desks, but nothing happened. “Doesn’t look like anyone is hiding here.”

“But if no one is hiding here, why spend so much on a set this large and detailed? The desks are carved with what looks like bloody writing, and someone deliberately arranged these old uniforms.” Zhu Jianing glanced behind him. “And the door opened by itself, almost like it was inviting us in.”

“Probably the wind.” Fei Youliang glared at him. “If you have time to mutter nonsense, help me find the mechanism.”

“Don’t get angry. I’m only analyzing the situation…” Zhu Jianing crossed the room. His broad frame knocked a uniform from a chair, but he stepped over the fallen cloth and continued toward the rear door. “There really is nothing to fear. I expected something to jump out while I passed the desks…”

Zhu Jianing’s voice faded. He turned and found the classroom restored to its original state.

“When I walked down the row, I remember knocking into one of the uniforms. Youliang, did you pick it up from the floor?”

“A uniform fell? I didn’t notice.” Fei Youliang stood several rows away at the opposite end of the classroom.

“Did I imagine it?” Zhu Jianing retraced his steps and stopped beside a desk at the center of the room. “I’m sure this was the one that fell.”

He lifted the uniform and shook it. A strange odor wafted from the cloth—the stench of rotten fish.

“That’s strange.” Zhu Jianing dropped the uniform on the desk and crouched to inspect the furniture for hidden mechanisms. Everything seemed solid. As he started to move on, something rattled inside the drawer like rolling marbles.

“There’s something inside?” Zhu Jianing bent down and leaned into the mouth of the drawer. The dark drawer was stuffed with test papers and textbooks.

“Why did it sound like marbles? Is there a hidden compartment?” He peered into the darkness and reached for the papers. The moment he removed the first sheet, two round eyes stared back at him.

“F*ck!” Half crouched, Zhu Jianing stumbled backward and knocked two desks out of place.

“What’s wrong?!” The commotion shocked Fei Youliang, who was also in the room.

“There’s someone in the drawer!” Zhu Jianing tried to scramble upright, but his limbs failed him. All color had drained from his face.

“Have you lost your mind?! How can a person fit inside a drawer?” Fei Youliang cursed as he went to help his teammate. “It’s probably some kind of prop.”

He pulled out the papers and textbooks from inside the drawer and dropped them onto the floor. “Take a look. Don’t be such a scaredy cat; there’s nothing inside.”

After ten seconds to calm himself down, Zhu Jianing finally climbed up from the floor. “But I really saw a pair of eyes… I’m not lying! I swear on my life!”

“Even if you did, it was only a Haunted House trick. Why panic?” Fei Youliang had not been particularly afraid, though Zhu Jianing’s certainty unsettled him. “Fine. Let’s leave this room for now.”

The pair fled, leaving chaos in their wake.

“Do we have to continue?” Zhu Jianing asked. The seemingly endless corridor made his heart tremble.

“You’re giving up after less than five minutes? We came to ruin this place, not advertise it.” Fei Youliang almost kicked him. “Pull yourself together! You have all those muscles, and you’re trembling like a child?”

Fei Youliang marched on. Frightened as he was, Zhu Jianing feared abandonment—and being branded a traitor to Qin Guang’s studio—even more, so he followed.

As he moved forward, he looked over his shoulder. When he saw the door to the sealed classroom slowly open again, he quickly caught up to Fei Youliang and hissed, “Let’s go, it feels like something is coming out from that classroom!”

The pair hurried on, passing the restroom and reaching the first junction.

“Just how big is this set? There’s even a choice of paths?”

Zhu Jianing had lost all confidence, and Fei Youliang’s brow furrowed. He had visited countless Haunted Houses, but none like this. They had not seen a single employee in costume, yet the fear refused to fade. The longer they stayed, the stronger it grew.

In other Haunted Houses, seeing the “ghosts” actually reassured him. They were merely costumed actors, visible proof that everything around him was artificial.

This place overturned every expectation. No actors had appeared, yet suspense saturated the air, as though something terrible might happen at any moment.

“Let’s try this way.”

The corridor narrowed as Fei Youliang and Zhu Jianing headed toward the girls’ dormitory.

The first few rooms proved harmless, and the tension in their chests gradually eased. Then they entered the Pen Spirit room.

The girls’ bedroom had been preserved like a crime scene. Four chairs stood side by side; several sheets of white paper and a ballpoint pen patched together with tape rested on one seat.
